findings.reason: pyproject.toml uses hatchling.build and has no [project.optional-dependencies]; the dev extra exists only in setup.py extras_require, which Hatchling ignores. requirements-dev.in (pytest, pytest-asyncio, ruff, black) is never installed, so a fresh container cannot run tests/ and the README's claim that all dependencies are installed is false. Lowered from high to medium: it breaks only the dev environment, not runtime behaviour.
findings.claim: postCreateCommand installs '.[dev]', but the project defines no dev extra that the build backend reads, so pytest and the other dev tools are never installed in the container.
findings.evidence: postCreateCommand installs '.[dev]', but pyproject.toml selects hatchling.build and defines no dev optional dependency. The dev extra in setup.py is not read by Hatchling, and requirements-dev.in is never installed. In a fresh container, the setup therefore omits pytest and pytest-asyncio, which tests/test_server.py requires.

findings.reason: devcontainer.json:7 sets workspaceFolder and line 20 sets python.defaultInterpreterPath to /workspaces/ProxmoxMCP-Plus, with no workspaceMount. The default mount is /workspaces/<checkout folder name>, so a renamed clone gets a missing workspace and a broken venv path. Lowered to low because the README's own clone command (README.md:95-96) creates a folder named ProxmoxMCP-Plus, so the default path works.
findings.claim: workspaceFolder and the interpreter path are hard-coded to /workspaces/ProxmoxMCP-Plus with no workspaceMount, so a checkout in a folder with a different name opens a directory that doesn't exist.
findings.evidence: workspaceFolder is fixed to /workspaces/ProxmoxMCP-Plus without a workspaceMount override. A checkout named proxmox-dev is mounted by default at /workspaces/proxmox-dev, leaving the configured workspace and postCreateCommand working directory nonexistent. Line 20 also fixes the interpreter to the unmatched path.
